summary: Independently reran all twelve R2 scope controls against exact Git source and added one narrow root-metadata/cleanup control. All thirteen controls pass twice with byte-identical outputs. R2 C11 now suppresses unsafe root status/signal/pid/error metadata, including getter exceptions and unsafe values at either snapshot; unknown metadata blocks completion and P2 selection. Existing R1 closures and all frozen product/test/workflow/evidence boundaries remain intact. This authorizes only scope transport of the reviewed exact diagnostic source, not product/native/release acceptance or any worker push.

independence.basis: Supporting critic independently read the exact Git diff/source/spec/state and original R1/R2 evidence. The critic did not implement the CLI. Controls are independently owned and execute actual extracted source functions in fresh VM contexts with virtual files/processes/streams. Generator control claims are not used as acceptance evidence.

sourceBinding.evidence: C01 requires the supplied exact R3 ref and known SHA-256, confirms HEAD, parent, unique tree, entire tracked diff empty, and disk script hash equal to Git source. Both final outputs report sourceUnchangedDuringControls=true.
sourceBinding.scopeConclusion: Only the approved new CLI revision and new parity-generator-r3 report/check artifacts changed. The R3 source correction is limited to root return metadata snapshots, safe stop metadata, unknown provenance and completion.

evidence: native-runtime-parity.mjs:42-54 reconstructs pid/status/signal from explicit numeric ranges and SAFE_SIGNALS, returning only null plus unknown=true for unsafe values or getter exceptions; it does not mutate native child objects.
native-runtime-parity.mjs:435-455 snapshots at launch and finish, preserves either unknown indication, and propagates unsafe launch error metadata as unknown without raw values.

native-runtime-parity.mjs:457-463 admits owned-handle stopping only from valid active metadata; 499-509 separates root-return-metadata-unknown cleanup basis and requires null signal/no metadata unknown/no launch error before diagnostic completion.

C11 reexecutes the original root signalCode, exitCode, pid, error.code and close-event status/signal canaries. None appear in any exported artifact. The previously leaking signal/status properties are rebuilt as null and cannot yield diagnosticCompleted=true.

C11 additionally executes throwing getters for all three root properties, an unsafe first getter value followed by normal finish, and a safe launch followed by an unsafe finish for each property. All thirteen unsafe-source cases yield rootMetadataUnknown=true, productResultUnknown=true, classification=diagnostic-incomplete-provenance-unknown, diagnosticCompleted=false and separate root-return-metadata-unknown cleanup basis.

The close-event canary case remains unused and is not exported; valid native root properties retain a complete diagnostic observation in that case. No metadata source is silently relabeled a product failure.

C13 verifies normal native object identity/content unchanged, three valid numeric/null/signal range shapes and 23 invalid-value shapes. Known signal and known launch error remain incomplete without inventing metadata or cleanup failure; legal null status yields unconfirmed cleanup, not unsafe-metadata provenance.

controlEvidence.topic: Single-key arms, common guard, budgets and fairness
controlEvidence.evidence: E0-E4 change exactly their single designated key and cross old trace off/on. Both forms retain the minimum guard. Host env/credentials/profile fixtures do not enter child env. E4 remains the SystemRoot-derived built-in module path; no combined arm. Fixed 600s/40s/3s reserve/10s/38/76 limits and worst-case admission are unchanged; virtual total76/smoke30 denies binding rather than raising budgets, while both parent forms precede fair remaining analog admission.

Normal/logger-stat/logger-append/health-failure/native-throw/sync-throw mocks preserve exact native returns/exceptions and unhandled ordinary error behavior. Common guard has no data observer. Only active owned handles are stopped; closed handles and historical PIDs are not signaled. Guard enforces launch caps, synchronous PowerShell refusal and counter logger fail-closed. taskkill128 is never interpreted as whole-tree or product cleanup proof.

Lifetime expiry, launch-budget abort, watchdog and output-limit independently remain reached=false/diagnostic-budget-not-reached/productResultUnknown=true, with cleanup unknown separately represented and no product failure inference.
